newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex inaugurates new Tula refinery unit.
newsitem.headline: Pemex inaugurates new Tula refinery unit.

text.p: Mexico's new hydrodesulphurization unit in its Tula refinery will have the capacity to produce 42,000 barrels per day (bpd) of fuel oil with low sulphur content, state-owned Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said on Monday.
The plant was inaugurated here on Monday.

The plant required an investment of $627 million, and was constructed by a consortium involving an Italian company, SNAM Progetti, which is controlled ENI group and two Mexican companies, ICA and Tribasa, Pemex said in a statement.
"With the operation of this complex, Pemex Refineries... will resolve basic problems of residuals, and sulphur content will be reduced from 3.5 to 1.0 percent," Pemex said.
Pemex said the new hydrodesulphurization unit "will eliminate the emission of 347 tonnes of sulphur per day in the atmosphere."
The Japanese ambssador to Mexico, Terusuki Terada, said that the Japanese government provided technical, environmental and financial assistance to the project.
